#EXP-1950: WHICH INSTALLS AN INSTALL TRUSTS (the pin store), how a new install is approved and a lost account reset, and the FOUR ACCEPTANCE RULES in RECORD-ONLY mode for release 1. Decisions by Danny 2026-11-24 on the issue: (a) a new install is trusted by a confirmation on an already trusted install, the first install trusts itself; (b) every trusted install lost = a reset, confirmed by a team-mate with the same row; (c) keys an install already holds stay trusted (`legacy`), holders sign the current epoch again (wrap-signature.json `resign`); (d) release 1 signs and RECORDS, unsigned is refused only in a later release (a BUILD constant `mode`, never a server flag). TS reference packages/domain-contract/src/install-trust.ts; every platform replays THIS file (desktop/CLI through enet-core, iOS, Android, web). Builds on wrap-signature.json (the wrap signature, `acceptWrap`, `acceptVouch`) and install-register.json (the registration message). Every value here is generated from `keys` (identity bytes 0x10.., 0x30.., ... in steps of one) so a replay needs no state.

THE CODE (`code`, `installCode`): an install that waits for approval shows 10 Crockford base32 characters (`alphabet`, no I L O U) in two groups of five, `XXXXX XXXXX`: the first 50 bits of SHA-256(`code.label` ‖ 0x00 ‖ endpointId[32 bytes]), most significant first. The trusted side derives the same code from the endpoint id of the row; NEITHER side ever reads a code from the server. The person compares the two codes; that comparison is the protection.

THE APPROVALS (`approval`, `approvalMessage`): ed25519 by the APPROVER's eNet identity (strict, as wrap-signature.json) over 125 bytes: `approval.label` ‖ 0x00 ‖ kind u8 (`kinds`) ‖ SHA-256(subject userId utf8)[32] ‖ subject endpointId[32] ‖ subject x25519Public[32]; signature = base64url without padding (86 chars). `root` = an install starts its account's chain, signed by ITSELF (approver = subject: the first install, and the new install of a reset); `approve` = a trusted install of the SAME account approves a new one; `reset` = a team-mate's trusted install confirms a member's new root; `decline` = this account turns a member's reset down (a Reset row's Remove). The subject's user, endpoint and X25519 key come from its row and count only when its REGISTRATION verifies (`registrationValid`, install-register.json's message over the stored `registrationSignature` + `registrationSignedAt`); an approval of a row whose registration does not verify is ignored.

THE SERVER (stores and relays, decides nothing about trust): `installs.trust {installId}` answers `installs` (every live install of the caller's account and of the members of the caller's teams: installId, userId, endpointId, x25519Public, registrationSignature, registrationSignedAt, approvalRequested, label) and `approvals` (kind, subjectEndpointId, approverEndpointId, signature) about them; `installs.requestApproval {installId}` marks an install that follows this rule and is not trusted (`approvalRequested`); `installs.claimRoot {installId, signature}` stores a `root` (CONFLICT while another live install of the account has a `root` or `approve`); `installs.approve {installId, subjectInstallId, kind: approve | reset | decline, signature}` stores one (approve: a subject of the caller's account; reset / decline: a team-mate's); `installs.waiting {}` = the Needs-you source: the own account's installs that asked and have no approval, and team-mates' `root` claims of a user who had an earlier root, not yet reset-approved or declined by the caller's account. A client shows ONLY the rows `reconcileTrust` also yields. Remove on a New install = `installs.revoke` (which drops its wraps and rotates, sealed-content.json `rotation`); Remove on a Reset = `installs.approve {kind: decline}`. The server verifies every signature it is given against the caller's install (a bug catcher, not the protection).

THE PIN STORE (`TrustStore`, per account on each install beside its tree keys; web IndexedDB, desktop/CLI a 0600 file, iOS Keychain, Android the Keystore vault): `self`, `userId`, `joined` (placed in its account's chain), `pins` (endpoint id → userId, x25519Public, `via`, `by`), `members` (team-mates ever pinned: a new root of one is a Reset, never a first contact), `declined`, `roots` (per root: the highest VERIFIED epoch and per held epoch `verified` | `legacy` | `unsigned` | `refused-would-be`; a key held before the store existed is `legacy`). `reconcileTrust(store, installs.trust)` (`trustCases`, compare `after`, `status`, `rows` whole; `before` and `after` name installs by `keys`): (1) only rows whose registration verifies count; (2) SHRINK: a pin no longer served (revoked, member removed) or served with another user or X25519 key is dropped: the server can always shrink the set; (3) this install is pinned `self`; (4) JOIN, once: its own verified `root` → joined; else the shortest chain of verified `approve`s (approvers of its own account) from one of its account's verified roots down to it: every install on that path is pinned `chain`, joined; (5) declines by this account's pinned installs are remembered; (6) once joined: FIRST CONTACT with a team-mate (no pin of theirs, not in `members`): their verified roots are pinned `first` (on the server's word, once); then to a fixpoint: an `approve` by a pinned install of the SAME account pins its subject `approved` (by = the approver); a `reset` by ANY pinned install of ANOTHER user pins a member's verified root `reset`; a declined subject never; (7) ROWS, only when joined (`copy`): `newInstall` = an install of the own account that is not pinned and asked (`approvalRequested`) or claims a root; `reset` = a team-mate's verified root, not pinned, of a user in `members`, not declined; a team-mate's other new installs are NEVER rows (their own installs approve them). Rows sort New install first, then by endpoint id; each is drawn as `row` (the code is never truncated). STATUS: `trusted` (joined), `waiting` (its account has a chain it is not on: it shows the EmptyState `icon` `ui-private`, title `copy.waiting`, the code as its one line), `claimRoot` (no chain: it signs `root` for itself, `installs.claimRoot`, and is trusted next round). A new install of an account with a chain calls `installs.requestApproval` once. A reset = every other install of the account removed (revoked): the account has no chain, the new install claims a root; its team-mates' installs see a Reset row. The ROLLOUT: the first install of an account that runs this release claims the root; every other install, an existing one updated to this release included, asks and is approved once (decision a), keeping every key it holds (`legacy`, decision c).

THE FOUR RULES (`rules`; `stores` = the named stores the cases run against, `victim` = install A, joined, pinning A, B and the team-mate T1, verified epoch 1 of root 0123… and epoch 2 of root 2123…). Each case names what a build does NOW (`mode.release1` = `record`) and once signing is MANDATORY (`mode.release2`); compare both whole. R1 `keepWrap` (`keepCases`, a wrap `sessionKeys.mine` serves, of ANY epoch: old content stays readable): signed by a pinned install and verifying = kept `verified`; unsigned = kept `unsigned` now, refused once mandatory; signed by an UNPINNED install whose signature is its own = kept `refused-would-be` now, refused `unpinned` once mandatory; a signature that fails (also one naming a pinned signer), a malformed wrap, one that does not open = refused in EVERY mode (wrap-signature.json order: malformed > unsigned > unpinned > unopened > signature). R2 `sealEpochCheck`: an answer naming an epoch BELOW the root's highest verified one is refused `rollback` in every mode (it only ever bites where a verified epoch exists, so no released build is affected). R3 `sealTo` (`sealCases`, the root and key `sendTarget`, `publicKeys` or the synced row name): with a held secret of that epoch, only to ITS public key (`keyMismatch` otherwise, every mode), recorded as that key's record, and once mandatory only a `verified` or `legacy` key; without one, a `vouch` by a pinned install = `verified`, none = `unsigned` (sealed now, the send waits `noKey` once mandatory), one by an unpinned install that verifies = `refused-would-be` (sealed now, refused once mandatory), one that fails = refused in every mode. R4 `wrapTarget` (`targetCases`, every install this one wraps for: `pending`, a new key's readers, a rotation, a new root's seal; `roots` = the targets that claim a verified root): ONLY a joined install wraps for others (a waiting one wraps for itself only, `notTrusted`); a pinned target served with its pinned user and key = `verified`; a pinned endpoint served with another key = `keyMismatch`, a registration that does not verify = `registration`, both refused in every mode; a target that ASKED to be approved or claims a root and is not pinned = `unapproved`, refused NOW already (this is the waiting state: an unapproved install gets no wraps from installs that follow this rule); a target that never asked and claims no root (an older build, its registration possibly not stored yet) = `legacy`, wrapped now and refused once mandatory. A CALL'S KEY `callKey` (`callCases`): the secret of the (root, epoch) `sendTarget` names, from this install's keyring ONLY; `rollback` in every mode; nothing held = `noKey`; now any held key (its record says what it is), once mandatory only `verified` or `legacy`, else the call ends `no_key`.

A NEW ROOT (`newRoot`): a seal whose root the same send creates (`sessions.send {seal}`, `voice.callConversation {seal}`) CANNOT be signed: the signature covers the root id, which the server assigns in that send. Its wraps go UNSIGNED for the readers R4 allows; the maker keeps its key `verified` (it made it) and signs them through `sessionKeys.resign` as soon as the send answers the root id, and again on every holder pass until done; until then a reader records `unsigned` (refused once mandatory, and the reader waits `noKey` for the resign).

A MALICIOUS SERVER (`maliciousServer`, one entry per attack of the threat model, each case = the EXACT answers of a lying server (`answers`, by procedure) and the verdict `now` and `mandatory`, replayed through the rule `replay` names with the same inputs as that rule's case of the same `name`): 1 false epoch (`sessionKeys.mine` plants a wrap of a key the server made; `sessions.sendTarget` names it); 2 false public key before any wrap (`sessionKeys.publicKeys` with no vouch, the server's own vouch, a lifted real vouch, a vouch naming a pinned signer); 3 false reader (`sessionKeys.pending` + `installs.list` name the server's install Z: silent, asking, claiming a root, a pinned endpoint with Z's key, a registration that does not verify); 4 false call key (`sessions.sendTarget` names a planted (root, epoch)). The test doubles of every platform answer exactly these.

WHAT RECORD-ONLY NEVER FIXES (release 1; the protection starts with mandatory): the server strips signatures and every wrap reads `unsigned`, kept; it signs with its own install and the wrap reads `refused-would-be`, kept; so attacks 1, 2 and 4 still WORK and are only RECORDED. Attack 3 works through an install that looks like an older build (never asked, no root): wrapped as `legacy`. Only a signature that FAILS, a rollback below a verified epoch, a pinned endpoint with a swapped key and an install that asked and is not approved are refused now. EVEN MANDATORY never fixes: a person who approves without comparing the code; the first contact with a team-mate (pinned on the server's word); a NEW install's own view of its chain (it joins along the chain the server shows it: a server that hides the real chain makes it claim a root (its account's other installs then see a New install row), and one that fakes a chain and an approval by its own install Z gets the NEW install to trust Z, while the account's other installs never do); a pinned team-mate's install that works with the server signs a key for any root; a real signed OLD epoch served to an install that never verified the newer one; a false `clearTree` for a root never seen keyed; a false root that names another real root the install holds; a hidden revoke (the server keeps listing a revoked pinned install) until revokes are signed; withholding (chats wait, calls end `no_key`: nothing is read).

trustCases.name: the first install: its account has no chain, it claims the root
the first install after its root claim: trusted, pinned itself
a second install asks: waiting, it shows its code
the root sees the asking install as a New install row
approve: the root pins it, signed by itself
the approved install joins: the chain from the root to it
a third install, approved by the second: the root pins it through a pinned approver
remove: the install is revoked, no longer served: its pin is dropped
a forged approval (not the approver's signature) pins nothing: the row stays
an approval by an install that is not pinned pins nothing
a registration that does not bind the key: never pinned, never a row
an older build (never asked, no root): no row, no pin: a legacy target
a waiting install shows no rows and pins nobody
first contact with a team-mate: their root pinned as served, their approved install through it
a team-mate's further install without a pinned voucher: not pinned, no row (their own installs approve it)
a team-mate with no root yet (older builds): nobody pinned, no row
a member pinned before, every install lost, a new root: a Reset row
the reset approved by this install: pinned as reset
the reset approved by another pinned member's install: pinned for this install too
a reset declined by this account (the row's Remove): no row, never pinned, also when another member approves
a competing root of the own account (a server that hid the chain from it): a New install row

attack 1, a planted epoch 2: naming a pinned signer (B) with the server's signature
attack 1, a planted epoch 2: a real signature of B lifted from another wrap

attack 1 (R2): a real older epoch served as current, below the verified one

honest: a vouch by a pinned install

an older build of the own account (never asked, no registration kept)

newRoot.rule: A seal whose root the same send creates (sessions.send {seal}, voice.callConversation {seal}) cannot be signed: the signature covers the root id, which the server assigns in that send. Its wraps go UNSIGNED, for the readers wrapTarget allows (pinned + legacy in record mode); the maker keeps its own key as verified (it made it), and as soon as the send answers the root id it signs them through sessionKeys.resign (wrap-signature.json resign), again on every holder pass until done. Until then a reader records unsigned. Once mandatory, a reader refuses the unsigned wrap and waits (noKey) for the resign, which follows within one pass.

row.$comment: THE ROW of an install waiting for approval, the same tree ×4 (genUI core parts only, no new component, no new text style). One per row inside ONE Section: a Stack (vertical, gap sm) holding (1) a Row: title = the label (a team-mate's: their name · the label; no label = the code), subtitle = the code, trailing = ONE Badge (`copy.newInstall` / `copy.reset`, variant secondary); (2) a Stack (horizontal, gap sm) of two Buttons: `copy.approve` (size sm) then `copy.remove` (size sm, variant ghost). The buttons never share the Row's line: with three trailing parts a 320 pt row left the code about 70 px and cut it (iOS #3413, web before). THE CODE IS NEVER TRUNCATED: down to 320 pt width it shows all 10 characters and the space; only the title may truncate. The waiting state: THE page EmptyState, icon `icon`, title `copy.waiting`, description = the code.
